event time line:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESOB Grade-II on \u0026amp; off since 20 Years (exacerbations once in a year)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased frequency \u0026amp; decreased urine output since 2 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical localization:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELungs - COPD - SOB Grade- II\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECOPD - PAH - RHF - Pedal edema \u0026amp; SOB Grade -IV\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrimary etiology:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECOPD (Biomass exposure)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) What are mechanism of action, indication and efficacy over placebo of each of the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used for this patient?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAugmentin:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAzithromycin:\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMechanism of action and indications\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK557766\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAzithromycin, like other macrolide antimicrobials, binds to the 23S portion of the 50S bacterial ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by preventing the transit of aminoacyl-tRNA and the growing protein through the ribosome. Compared to erythromycin, azithromycin is less prone to disassociation from the Gram-negative ribosome, conferring its greater efficacy against Gram-negative pathogens.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIndications:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECommunity-acquired Pneumonia. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPharyngitis or Tonsillitis. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUncomplicated skin\/skin structure. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute bacterial exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute bacterial sinusitis. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGenital Ulcer Disease (Chancroid) ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENongonococcal or Gonococcal Urethritis and Cervicitis. ...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPelvic Inflammatory Disease.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEfficacy of Azithromycin over placebo\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.dovepress.com\/the-belgian-trial-with-azithromycin-for-acute-copd-exacerbations-requi-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-COPD\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHydrocortisone\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/annalsofintensivecare.springeropen.com\/articles\/10.1186\/s13613-014-0032-x\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Head end Elevation:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESignificantly increases global and regional end-expiratory lung volume. It has also been shown to improve oxygenation and hemodynamic performance.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.BiPAP:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy having a custom air pressure for when you inhale and a second custom air pressure when you exhale, the machine is able to provide relief to your overworked lungs and chest wall muscles.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo correct respiratory acidosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Chest physiotherapy:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is a term used for a group of treatments designed to improve respiratory efficiency, promote expansion of the lungs, strengthen respiratory muscles, and eliminate secretions from the respiratory system.It includes postural drainage, chest percussion, chest vibration, turning, deep breathing exercises, and coughing\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) What could be the causes for her current acute exacerbation?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4. Could the ATT have affected her symptoms? If so how?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.What could be the causes for her electrolyte imbalance?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7544412\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;2) Neurology (10 Marks)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA) Link to patient details:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/143vibhahegde.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/wernickes-encephalopathy.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESymptomatology \u0026amp; event time line:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChronic alcoholic since 12 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiabetes since 2 yrs (irregular medications)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2-3 episodes of seizures in last 1 year\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIrrelevant talking , forgetfulness and decreased food intake since 9 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical localization:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBrain : Wernicke's Encephalopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKidney : AKI (pre-renal sec to ?dehydration)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrimary etiology:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh2RLYF38pPeFc5PB01t3rwjoWDYTqzIX5hWDSo3zFNFAx3LYVAQHBjt9S11bfVegiPWr15v-M57z5Aa9D95I72X8PxGwE3RK_givlbbpo6rNIqwBvTFABoGw7WyNxX7ChhOVP4XcdgZ_o\/s1605\/Screenshot_20210619-093631__01.jpg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1605\" data-original-width=\"1440\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh2RLYF38pPeFc5PB01t3rwjoWDYTqzIX5hWDSo3zFNFAx3LYVAQHBjt9S11bfVegiPWr15v-M57z5Aa9D95I72X8PxGwE3RK_givlbbpo6rNIqwBvTFABoGw7WyNxX7ChhOVP4XcdgZ_o\/s320\/Screenshot_20210619-093631__01.jpg\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/arcr.niaaa.nih.gov\/binge-drinking-predictors-patterns-and-consequences\/binge-drinkings-effects-body\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)\u0026nbsp; Mechanism of action, indication and efficacy over placebo of each of the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used for this patient?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThiamine: correction of thiamine deficiency\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7163251\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKCL \u0026amp; Potchlor: correction of hypokalemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/emedicine.medscape.com\/article\/242008-treatment#d9\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELorazepam: to treat alcohol withdrawl\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4606320\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Why have neurological symptoms appeared this time, that were absent during withdrawal earlier? What could be a possible cause for this?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis time he may have developed wernicke's encephalopathy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOr it may be due to uremic encephalopathy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOr it may because of kindling in alcohol withdrawl where repeated withdrawls will lead to more severe symptoms.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/europepmc.org\/article\/PMC\/6761822\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) What is the reason for giving thiamine in this patient?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis patient may had thiamine deficiency secondary to chronic alcoholism which is causing wernicke's encephalopathy by various mechanisms.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThiamine supplementation will lead to improvement of the symptoms and often complete resolution in some cases.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThiamine administration is usually continued until clinical improvement ceases.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERecovery from the ophthalmoplegia was complete after a few hours, except for a residual, fine, horizontal nystagmus in 60% of patients. Recovery from ataxia occurred after a few days, although in some cases was incomplete. The changes in mental status tended to improve after 2–3 weeks of therapy.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.thelancet.com\/journals\/laneur\/article\/PIIS1474-4422%2807%2970104-7\/references\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5) What is the probable reason for kidney injury in this patient?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol - osmotic diuresis - dehydration - pre renal AKI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.healthline.com\/health\/does-alcohol-dehydrate-you#\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6). What is the probable cause for the normocytic anemia?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol abuse and dependence can cause normocytic normochromic anemia through:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecreased red blood cell production in the bone marrow - Normocytic normochromic anemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoss of blood through ulcers or inflammation - Iron deficiency anemia which in normocytic normochromic in early stages\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDestruction of red blood cells from heart valve issues, inflammation, immune system damage, or a cancerous tumor - Normocytic normochromic anemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.alcohol.org\/effects\/anemia\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7) Could chronic alcoholism have aggravated the foot ulcer formation? If yes, how and why?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChronic alcoholism may lead to foot ulcer formation and delayed healing due to alcoholic neuropathy \u0026amp; malnutrition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB) Link to patient details:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/kausalyavarma.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/a-52-year-old-male-with-cerebellar.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESymptomatology \u0026amp; event time line:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChronic alcoholic \u0026amp; smoker since 30 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGiddiness \u0026amp; the reason for this patient to develop ataxia in the past 1 year?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGoing by the history in this patient ataxia may be secondary Does Alcoholism contribute to bleeding diatheses ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMost commonly IC bleed is secondary to Trauma or Hypertension.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGoing by the history there is no recent fall (trauma).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe is not a known hypertensive either but his ECG is showing features suggestive of LVH (SOKOLOW-LYON CRITERIA : S - wave in V1 + R - wave in V5\/V6 \u0026gt; 35 mm)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWhich may be secondary to chronic HTN (undiagnosed).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESo in this patient based on the data available IC bleed may be secondary to previously undiagnosed HTN.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOr\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHeavy alcohol consumption which was associated with increased risk of intracerebral hemorrhage.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.researchgate.net\/publication\/316523838_Alcohol_use_and_risk_of_intracerebral_hemorrhage\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol \u0026amp; bleeding diathesis:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol (ethanol) intake has effects on platelet aggregation and activation, coagulation factors including von Willebrand factor (vWF), and the fibrinolytic system.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWith regard to the effect of alcohol on platelet function, evidence in the literature suggests both platelet activation and platelet inhibition by ethanol. A unifying hypothesis is that platelets are partially activated by ethanol, with partial degranulation allowing for continued circulation of platelets with impaired function. Evidence also exists showing that ethanol intake decreases fibrinogen, factor VII, and vWF levels. In addition, alcohol intake has been found to increase fibrinolysis by increasing tissue plasminogen activator activity.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.researchgate.net\/publication\/7659399_Effects_of_Alcohol_on_Hemostasis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EF) Link to patient details:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttp:\/\/shivanireddymedicalcasediscussion.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/a-30-yr-old-male-patient-with-weakness.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Does the patient's history of road traffic accident have any role in his present condition?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo it doesn't\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.What are warning signs of CVA?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.neuroskills.com\/brain-injury\/stroke\/what-are-the-signs-and-symptoms-of-a-stroke\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.What is the drug rationale in CVA?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4. Does alcohol has any role in his attack?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEpidemiological evidence indicates that recent heavy alcohol consumption increases the risk for all major types of stroke, whereas light-to-moderate alcohol intake is associated with a decreased risk of ischemic stroke.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe pathophysiologic mechanisms by which alcohol triggers the onset of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage, aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage and ischemic brain infarction remain largely unresolved.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe effects of alcohol on hemostasis, fibrinolysis and blood clotting are variable and could either prevent or promote the occurrence of strokes. Regular light-to moderate alcohol consumption seems to afford protection against atherogenesis via several possible mechanisms.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/documentcloud.adobe.com\/link\/review?uri=urn:aaid:scds:US:32bf4e92-ca76-4e0d-973d-f21152c018e0\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.Does his lipid profile has any role for his attack??\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHis lipid profile is with in normal limits - no role in his current problem\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/amishajaiswal03eloggm.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/a-50-year-old-patient-with-cervical.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E__*Questions*_\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)What is myelopathy hand ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is loss of power of adduction and extension of the ulnar two or three fingers and an inability to grip and release rapidly with these fingers.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThese changes have been termed \"myelopathy hand\" and appear to be due to pyramidal tract involvement in various cervical spinal disorders when there is involvement of the spinal cord.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIntrinsic muscle wasting \u0026amp; positive finger escape present.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3818752\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)What is finger escape ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWartenberg's sign is a neurological sign consisting of involuntary abduction of the fifth (little) finger, caused by unopposed action of the extensor digiti minimi.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis finding of weak finger adduction in cervical myelopathy is also called the \"finger escape sign\".\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)What is Hoffman’s reflex?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHoffmann's reflex (Hoffmann's sign, sometimes simply \"Hoffmann's\", also finger flexor reflex) is involuntary flexion movement of the thumb and or index finger when the examiner flicks the fingernail of the middle finger down. The reflexive pathway causes the thumb to flex and adduct quickly.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA positive Hoffman sign indicates an upper motor neuron lesion and corticospinal pathway dysfunction likely due to cervical cord compression.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHowever, up to 3% of the population has been found to have a positive Hoffman without cord compression or upper motor neuron disease.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr Beta blockers also help open up your veins and arteries to improve blood flow.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIndications: it is used to treat Angina, High blood pressure and to lower the risk of hear attacks.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) What are the indications and contraindications for PCI?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINDICATIONS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon–ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUnstable angina.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStable angina.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnginal equivalent (eg, dyspnea, arrhythmia, or dizziness or syncope)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHigh risk stress test findings.\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECONTRAINDICATIONS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIntolerance for oral antiplatelets long-term.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAbsence of cardiac surgery backup.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHypercoagulable state.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHigh-grade chronic kidney disease.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChronic total occlusion of SVC.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAn artery with a diameter of \u0026lt;1.5 mm.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) What happens if a PCI is performed in a patient who does not need it? What are the harms of over treatment and why is research on over testing and over treatment important to current healthcare systems?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOver diagnosis is which occurs when a true abnormality is discovered, but detection of that abnormality and its treatment does not benefit the patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOver diagnosis will lead to over treatment , psychological effects \u0026amp; economic burden.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7586591\/#\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo prevent these adverse events more research is important in this over diagnosis \u0026amp; over treatment.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/bhavaniv.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/case-discussion-on-myocardial-infarction.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESymptomatology \u0026amp; profuse sweating since 1 day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical localization:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHeart : Inferior wall MI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrimary etiology:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute inferior wall MI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ET2DM , HTN leading to CAD.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECLINICAL INDICATIONS OF PTCA:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute ST - elevation myocardial infarction ( STEMI )\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon ST - elevation acute coronary syndrome ( NSTE-ACS )\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUnstable angina\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStable angina\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnginal equivalent (eg; dyspnoea, arrhythmia, or dizziness or syncope )\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHigh risk stress test findings.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/kattekolasathwik.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/a-case-of-cardiogenic-shock.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. event time line:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChronic alcoholic since 9 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPain abdomen \u0026amp; vomiting 5 yrs back - treated conservatively\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStopped alcohol for 3 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAgain started drinking from last 1 year\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERecurrent episodes (5-6) of pain abdomen \u0026amp; vomiting in last 1 year\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased alcohol consumption since last 20 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELast binge 1 week back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPain abdomen \u0026amp; vomiting since 1 week\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFever , burning micturition \u0026amp; constipation since 4 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECourse in hospital:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdmitted in hospital and treated conservatively\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3-4 days later clinical deterioration with SIRS (tachypnea , tachycardia (SVT) , leucocytosis , fever , SOB)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMalecot drains were placed for psuedocyst \u0026amp; peripancreatic collections\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EICD was placed for left sided hydropneumothorax\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEscalation of antibiotics \u0026amp; other symptomatic treatment continued\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClinical improvement with resolution of symptoms and was discharged in a hemodynamically stable state 10 days later\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical localization :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Pancreas\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Lungs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrimary etiology:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EALCOHOL\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPancreatitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPseudocyst \u0026amp; peri pancreatic collections\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPancreatico pleural fistula\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPleural effusion(exudative)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBroncho pleural fistula\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHydropneumothorax.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/nehae-logs.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/case-discussion-on-25-year-old-male.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) What is causing the patient's dyspnea? How is it related to pancreatitis?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient has mild b\/l pleural effusion which may be causing his dyspnea.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETwo main causes of pleural effusion are:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Transdiaphragmatic lymphatic blockage leading to increased permiability.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Pancreaticopleural fistulae secondary to leak and disruption of the pancreatic duct or pseudocyst caused by an episode of acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThese changes are mediated by inflammatory cytokines.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESpecific markers for Alcoholic Liver Disease:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•AST level is more than twice that of ALT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Elevated levels of Gamma Glutamyl Transferase (GGT)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/chennabhavana.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/general-medicine-case-discussion-1.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) what is the most probable diagnosis in this patient?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERuptured liver abscess\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOrganized collection secondary to hollow viscus perforation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) What was the cause of her death?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESEPSIS with MODS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBut again etiology can be confirmed only by exploratory laporotomy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Does her NSAID abuse have something to do with her condition? How?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIf at all it is a hollow viscus perforation it can be secondary to her NSAID abuse.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.medscape.com\/viewarticle\/437220#:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENSAID abuse may lead to grade-3 RPD changes in kidney\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECKD (?Analgesic Nephropathy)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5) Nephrology (and Urology) 10 Marks\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA) Link to patient details:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/kavyasamudrala.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/medicine-case-discussion-this-is-online.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Why doesn't the child have the excessive urge of urination at night time ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere the child has excessive urge to urinate during day time even though bladder isn’t full because of his psychological impulse to urinate.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDuring night time as he is asleep he wouldn’t have compulsion to do so.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPsychosomatic overactive bladder\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere the cause of overactive bladder is a condition called pollakiuria, or frequent daytime urination syndrome. Children who have pollakiuria urinate frequently. In some cases, they may urinate every five to 10 minutes or urinate between 10 and 30 times a day. This condition is most common among children aged 3 to 8 and is present only during waking hours. There are no other symptoms present. Doctors believe that pollakiuria is related to stress.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.webmd.com\/urinary-incontinence-oab\/overactive-bladder-in-children\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. How would you want to manage the patient to relieve him of his symptoms?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is usually unnecessary to treat pollakiuria. The symptoms should subside within a few weeks of starting. In some cases, however, it may take 7-12 months to clear up completely.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is also helpful to try to identify possible triggers \u0026amp; avoid them.A trigger could be anything that causes the child stress.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPsychological counselling can be done.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6) Infectious Disease (HI virus, Mycobacteria, Gastroenterology, Pulmonology) 10 Marks\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA) Link to patient details:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/vyshnavikonakalla.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/a-40-year-old-lady-with-dysphagia-fever.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;1.Which clinical history and physical findings are characteristic of tracheo esophageal fistula?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn this patient perse there are no definitive clinical signs\/symptoms characteristic of TEF except for regurgitation \u0026amp; Do you think drinking locally made alcohol caused liver abscess in this patient due to predisposing factors present in it ?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAmoebic liver abscess (ALA ) seen commonly in the tropics is predominantly confined to adult males, especially those who consume locally brewed alcohol, although intestinal amoebiasis occurs in all age groups and in both genders.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt has been argued that socioeconomic factors and poor sanitary conditions are the primary culprits that casually link alcohol to ALA.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHowever , there has emerged an abundance of data that implicates alcohol in a more causal role in facilitating the extra-intestinal invasion of the infective protozoan and the subsequent development of ALA.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWhat could be the cause in this patient ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E## Hence the consumption of locally brewed alcohol is the most likely cause of Liver abscess in this patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC6077556\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Steroids reduce inflammation in the lungs for Co-19 and appear to help stop some of the damage that can happen when the body's immune system goes into overdrive to fight off coronavirus. What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization for his current problem based on the clinical findings?How specific is his dilated superficial Abdominal vein in making diagnosis?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Based on the clinical symptoms and signs, the clinical diagnosis of the patient can be-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUTI with cirrhosis of liver with portal hypertension.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb) What is the etiology of the current problem and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis? What is the cause of his hypoalbuminemia?Why is the SAAG low?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-The etiology of the disease in this patient could be a chronic history of alcoholism. Chronic smoking leading to his apthous ulcers.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBased on his clinical finding there could be portal hypertension which could have been preceeded by cirrhosis of liver which might have been caused due to chronic alcoholism.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECirrhosis of liver leads to reduced protein synthesis thereby leading to decreased serum albumin levels causing hypoalbuminemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec)Will PT,INR derangement preceed hypoalbuminemia in liver dysfunction??Share reference articles if any!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-The liver plays a central role in the clotting process, and acute and chronic liver diseases are invariably associated with coagulation disorders due to multiple causes: decreased synthesis of clotting and inhibitor factors, decreased clearance of activated factors, quantitative and qualitative platelet defects, hyperfibrinolysis, and accelerated intravascular coagulation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.medscape.com\/answers\/177354-36077\/what-is-the-role-of-prothrombin-time-pt-in-the-evaluation-of-acute-liver-failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ed)What is the etiology of his fever and pancytopenia?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;e)Can there be conditions with severe hypoalbuminemia but no pedal edema? Can one have hereditary analbuminemia and yet have minimal edema? Please go this article https:\/\/www.frontiersin.org\/articles\/10.3389\/fgene.2019.00336\/full and answer the question.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInflammation and infection\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlbumin is considered a negative acute phase reactant, which means that as inflammation and other acute physiologic processes occur, its levels decrease\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn liver disease:Albumin is synthesized in the liver, and low serum albumin can be indicative of liver failure or diseases such as cirrhosis and chronic hepatitis. If present, hypoalbuminemia is generally considered to be a sign of advanced hepatic cirrhosis, or irreversible damage to the liver\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMalnutrition or malabsorption\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELow albumin levels can also indicate chronic malnutrition from protein losing enteropathy.[3] This is often caused or exacerbated by ulcerative colitis,[10] but can also be seen in cardiac disease and systemic lupus erythematosus.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConditions with severe hypoalbuminemia and no pedal edema- There can be a compensatory synthesis of protiens (globulins) other than albumin and thereby maintain the oncotic pressure in the intravascular compartment and preventing the extravasation of fluid. This could also be possible if there is a hypovolemic state in the same patient with hypoalbuminemia so that the pressures are again maintained and there is no fluid accumulation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is possible for one with hereditary analbuminemia to not have pedal edema. Since it is a chronic and hereditary disease there can be compensatory synthesis of other plasma proteins.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ef) What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in his current treatment plan\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns: tamsulosin efficacy in UTI patients\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.α1-Adrenergic receptor antagonists are used by 80% of physicians as the first agent to treat patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS); 27 of 30 clinical trials have confirmed that α-blockers are effective for BPH treatment.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Tamsulosin's α1A subtype adrenergic receptor selectivity is considered to be responsible for its low cardiovascular side effects and lack of interaction with antihypertensives.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.A 4-year extension, multicenter, open-label, phase IIIB clinical study evaluated long-term efficacy, safety, and tolerability of tamsulosin for up to 6 years; the study found a consistent statistically significant improvement in AUA symptom scores over 6 years, and most patients showed improvement during the first year that was sustained over 6 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.The low incidence of acute urinary retention in patients treated with tamsulosin for up to 6 years suggests that tamsulosin may reduce the risk of AUR in patients with BPH.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.Response to treatment and incidence of adverse events (eg, rhinitis and abnormal ejaculation) in patients with hypertension, diabetes, or nonhypertensive cardiovascular disease did not differ significantly from that in those without.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.Abnormal ejaculation is an important side effect of tamsulosin, but it resulted in few discontinuations during treatment. It may not always be deemed important by patients, and was not linked to complaints of decreased libido, impotence, or other changes in sexual function.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC1477608\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENitrofurantoin efficacy:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhb2GxPoG29dMRD6Q-GEb0iUh6A_Q8-MoUfevZ1D212289CV4h7bAMw0udO93WWp1RDMdIo_ExxgaaWoHLlo297C0LSgoybXyALOrgRz2MYjlrZ9eNnaooPClJZBvcZgNOewTWLJV_rTYU\/s1368\/Screenshot_20210323-065956__01.jpg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1368\" data-original-width=\"1334\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhb2GxPoG29dMRD6Q-GEb0iUh6A_Q8-MoUfevZ1D212289CV4h7bAMw0udO93WWp1RDMdIo_ExxgaaWoHLlo297C0LSgoybXyALOrgRz2MYjlrZ9eNnaooPClJZBvcZgNOewTWLJV_rTYU\/s320\/Screenshot_20210323-065956__01.jpg\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ecomparing 3 days of nitrofurantoin with placebo in young women with symptoms of UTI and pyuria found clinical cure rates of 70% versus 42%, respectively, 7 days after the start of therapy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe prevalence of participants with side effects attributed to nitrofurantoin in the 17 studies generally ranged from 5% to 16%; nausea, abdominal discomfort and headaches were described. An exception was an open-label randomized controlled trial whose primary outcome was quality of life.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/academic.oup.com\/jac\/article\/70\/9\/2456\/721364\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQUESTION 2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E45year old female with abdominal distension\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/navyamallempalli.blogspot.com\/2021\/02\/dr_6.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ea). What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization for her current problem based on the clinical findings?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROBLEM REPRESENTATION:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Abdominal distension since 2years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.shortness of breath\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.pedal edema since 2 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.cachexia_malnourishment\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical localisation:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.abdominal distension : causes: fluid,fetus,flatus,fat,feaces\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere in this case:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EO\/E: flankfullness and fluid thrill is present __indicates distension is because of fluid_ASCITIS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn this case the pattern is ascitis followed by pedal edema _clinically it indicates problem is in .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOverall the major problem in this case_refractory ascitis since 2 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb) What is the etiology of her refractory ascites and pleural effusion? and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn this case ,ascitis recurs shortly after therapuetic paracentesis despite sodium restriction and diuretic treatment._refractory ascitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECAUSES OF REFRACTORY ASCITIS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Non compliance to treatment\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Tumor_hepatoma\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Renal thrombosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.NSAIDS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7.Infection\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E8.GI Bledding\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;On ascitic fluid analysis: It is high SAAG and low protein ,it probably due to portal hypertension.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;she is on diuretics,frequent therapeutic paracentesis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer RFT was normal _no renal failure,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENoincreased cell counts in ascitic fluid, no features of infection _rule out SBP\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo H\/O 7se of bleeding:melena,hemetemesis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESo in this case most probably ascitis due to portal hypertension :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDD: cirrhosis of liver\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESchistosomiasis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPortal vein outflow obstruction.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECirrhosis is ruled out clinically no symptoms like jaundice,no coagulation disorders,no other signs of liver cell failure radiologically no altered echotexture,no shrunken liver,no nodules .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStool microscopy was done to rule out schistosomiasis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPortal vein thrombosis evaluation done by triple phase cect followed byMR Venogram.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn triple phase CECT :Focal short segment of intrahepatic segment of IVC just below the diaphragm with normal hepaticveins And multiple osteosclerotic lesions in pelvis,ribs,vertebral bodies __sarcoidosis \/metastasis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMR Vengram_ suggested severe narrowing of intrahepatic portion of IVC___Chronic buud chiari Share the potential advantages and disadvantages of Peritoneal dialysis catheter placement in refractory ascites?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EManagement of BCS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Diagnosis of BCS made by clinical features, laboratory and radiological investigations , management of underlying cause\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Anti coagulant therapy with LMWH and then warfarin aim for INR 2_3\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Treat the complications of portal hypertension with spirinolactone ,furosemide,and gastroscopy for variceal screening and band ligation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.consider angioplasty \/stenting for venous obstruction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.consider TIPS if no improvement with anticoagulation , angioplasty, stenting.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.TIPS fails \/no improvement and acute liver failure consider liver transplantation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7.Monitor chronic BCS for HCC by 6 monthly USG and alpha fetoprotein.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EManagement of refractory ascitis :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization for his current problem based on the clinical findings?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Based on the clinical findings the problem in this patient is with his heart.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBased on the detailed history and clinical findings the provisional diagnosis would be- k\/c\/o cor pulmonale with severe pulmonary arterial hypertension grade III with gross ascitis with acute kidney injury.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb) What is the etiology of his ascites? and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis?Chart out the sequence of events!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-The reason for ascitis in this patient could be RHF. RHF leads to congestive hepatomegaly and thereby derranging the synthetic funtion of the liver to produce albumin. And hypoalbuminemia leads to fluid accumulation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAKI can also lead to ascitis due to increased salt and water retention.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECOPD----\u0026gt;RHF----\u0026gt; congestive hepatomegaly----\u0026gt; reduced protein synthesis----\u0026gt; ascitis due to fluid accumulation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecreased urine output---\u0026gt;AKI---\u0026gt; Salt and water retention ----\u0026gt; ascitis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec)What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in his treatment plan?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ed)What are his current outcomes ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- The patient can go in cardiopulmonary arrest.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization for his current problem based on the clinical findings?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA)chronic smoker and\u0026nbsp; tobacco chewer\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/o left lower limb fracture 2 years back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStarted 15 years ago, initially chewed 1 or 2 packs\/day \u0026amp; gradually increased to 3-4\/day and even 5-7 on a few days. What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization for his current problem based on the clinical findings?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA)progressive sob from grade 2 to 4 since 2 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eorthopnea,pnd\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb\/l pedal edema upto knee since 2 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneralised weakness since 2 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/o cva (rt hemiparesis recovered) with persistent loss of speech since 2 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eanatomical localisation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBased on history:pnd ,sob with orthopnea suggest left heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ebased on examination:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eshift of apex to 6th ics,presence of thrill palpable at apex(?s1), nature of the apex not mentioned\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Epresence of loud p2 ,dilated veins ,pedal edema,s3 in both apical and left parasternal areas.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E(?biventricular failure)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb) What is the etiology of the current problem and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of his problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiology:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECAD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEcg showing\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)normal axis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)pathological Q waves from v1 to v6\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)poor R wave progression\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Esuggest a CAD probably involving LAD and LCX territory\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Econfirmed with finding on the echo leading to heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec) What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in his current treatment plan\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)salt and fluid restriction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23787719\/#:~:text=Conclusion%3A%20Individualized%20salt%20and%20fluid,Quality%20of%20life%3B%20Salt%20restriction.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENinety-seven stable patients in NYHA class II-IV, on optimal medication, with previous signs of fluid retention, treated with either \u0026gt;40 mg (NYHA III-IV) or \u0026gt;80 mg (NYHA II-IV) of furosemide daily were randomized to either individualized salt and fluid restriction or information given by the nurse-led heart failure clinics, e.g. be aware not to drink too much and use salt with caution, and followed for 12 weeks. Fluid was restricted to 1.5 L and salt to 5 g daily, and individualized dietary advice and support was given.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EResults After 12 weeks, significantly more patients in the intervention than in the control group improved on the composite endpoint (51% vs. 16%; P \u0026lt; 0.001), mostly owing to improved NYHA class and leg oedema. No negative effects were seen on thirst, appetite, or QoL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)benfomet as thiamine replacement in alcoholic pts\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4550087\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)aldactone(spironolactone)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.aafp.org\/afp\/2001\/1015\/p1393.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBased on earlier work suggesting a benefit of therapy,2 the Randomized Aldactone Evaluation Study (RALES) was undertaken to evaluate the role of spironolactone when used in addition to standard therapy for CHF. Standard therapy in this study did not include beta blockers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;S-The investigators prospectively enrolled 1,663 patients with severe (New York Heart Association [NYHA] class IV) CHF (Table 1).4 Most of the enrolled patients were white men averaging 65 years of age. These patients had a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35 percent or less and marked physical limitations related to CHF. Patients were excluded if they had unstable angina or moderate renal failure, and if they were hyperkalemic.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAll patients who could tolerate the drug were given an ACE inhibitor and a loop diuretic, and 70 percent were taking digoxin. Only 10 percent were taking beta blockers. Patients were randomly assigned to receive placebo or 25 mg of spironolactone daily in addition to their current regimen. After eight weeks, if the patient showed worsening CHF and had a stable potassium level, the dosage was increased to 50 mg daily. The dosage was decreased to 25 mg every other day if at any time the patient became hyperkalemic\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/soumya9814.blogspot.com\/2021\/01\/this-is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ea) What is the problem representation of this patient and what is the anatomical localization?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA)52 year old\u0026nbsp; male diabetic and hypertensive with complains of SOB, cough ,decrease sleep and appetite since 10 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPure vegetarian with hb 5.7,macrocytes on smear suggesting Vit B12 deficiency and electrolyte imbalance\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical location\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Esob without pedal edema, pnd, orthopnea can be localised to the lung\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E(sob on exertion grade 2 can also be localised the heart but no history or examination finding of pedal edema or jvp rise rules it out\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ecough with sputum\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eb)What is the etiology of the current problem and how would you as a member of the treating team arrive at a diagnosis? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of his problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA)?Sub acute combined degeneration of spinal cord secondary to vit B12 deficiency.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E?Diabetic neuropathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E?Hypervolemic hyponatremia secondary to heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E?Pseudohyponatremia secondary to uncontrolled sugars\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec) What is the efficacy of each of the drugs listed in his current treatment plan especially for his hyponatremia? What is the efficacy of Vaptans over placebo? Can one give both 3% sodium as well as vaptan to the same patient?\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA)https:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/pii\/S0085253815551089\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETHE INDICATIONS FOR VAPTANS ARE NOT CLEAR\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1-First, we do not know how to distinguish between symptoms that are an indication for vaptan and those that are not.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2-Together, we lack information on which degree of severity of hyponatremia should give us reason to consider vaptan treatment.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3-Third, work by Gankam Kengne et al.28 suggested that patients with mild chronic hyponatremia fall to the ground more often than matched normonatremic controls .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWe are unable to answer the question of whether elderly patients with chronic mild hyponatremia should be treated, for example, by a vaptan to correct hyponatremia and prevent fractures.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4-Fourth, in terms of indication for vaptan, the area least controversial might appear to be that of severe symptomatic (chronic) hyponatremia. A ‘hyponatremia-naive’ physician is likely to conclude that vaptans if anything should be promising in severe symptomatic hyponatremia. However, there are literally no published data on this. Clinical trials of vaptans have consistently excluded severe symptomatic hyponatremia from study because of ethical concerns (risk of worsening of severe symptoms when receiving placebo)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Erecent expert panel suggested that in severe symptomatic (chronic) hyponatremia, infusions of hypertonic saline should have priority over vaptan.30 This is an area of significant uncertainty. It has been pointed out that 3% NaCl may correct hyponatremia too quickly,31 or it may occasionally lead to pulmonary edema in SIAD(H). On the other hand, we have personal experience (PAG) that SIAD(H)-related severe symptomatic hyponatremia is a rewarding indication for vaptan. Thus, in the absence of a trial comparing fluid restriction plus 3% saline with vaptans in severe symptomatic hyponatremia, we do not have a database to make specific recommendations for or against vaptans.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) Please mention your
